memory_update.text: YUM is the demand-side reference anchor for multi-brand procurement consolidation because external context directly states it is unifying supply-chain organization across its restaurant portfolio.
DPZ is a reference benchmark for vertically integrated restaurant procurement and distribution; it may help identify what third-party suppliers must replicate for other franchisors.

WEST should be tracked as an underfollowed B2B beverage/private-label supplier with possible national-account foodservice exposure, but restaurant-chain specificity still needs primary-source verification.

FARM is a speculative micro-cap exception with unusually direct claimed restaurant customer exposure, but post-asset-sale customer continuity, profitability, and scale must be verified before it can survive later Serenity layers.

This Layer 1B pass has not yet mapped non-beverage suppliers such as packaging, condiments, protein processors, specialty ingredients, cold-chain logistics, testing/inspection, or supplier-network software; later passes should search those categories deliberately.

node: Multi-brand procurement consolidation and approved supplier networks
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around multi-brand restaurant procurement consolidation. Reference lane names are Yum Brands, as a consolidating franchisor customer, and Domino's, as a vertically integrated procurement/supply-chain benchmark. Underfollowed discovery candidates are Westrock Coffee and Farmer Bros., both B2B/private-label coffee or beverage suppliers with plausible exposure to restaurant, foodservice, and national-account procurement networks. Farmer Bros. is included as a below-USD-300M speculative exception because the customer-supplier signal appears unusually direct, but its size and financial risk require stricter verification.
